office_does: One of two Washington State Representatives for the 46th District in northeast Seattle, serving a two-year term writing state law and budgets.
race_blurb: Incumbent Democrat Darya Farivar, who won about 89% of the primary vote, faces independent first-time candidate Rodney 'Star' Thornley, who has reported no fundraising.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative, King County ADA and disability-equity specialist, and the first Middle Eastern woman elected to the Legislature.
highlights: Passed legislation stopping stores from blocking new grocers and pharmacies, and legislation expanding the caregiver workforce [S1][S4][S5]
Campaign site backs a wealth tax and calls rent stabilization 'the most important legislation' on housing [S6]
Voted yes on ESSB 6346 (2026) and ESHB 1296 (2025) [S7][S8]

taxes.basis: Voted for ESSB 6346 and her campaign site supports a wealth tax.

housing.basis: Calls rent stabilization the most important housing legislation, alongside support for missing-middle housing.

safety.basis: Police-accountability coalition board member; cites behavioral-health response teams and AG police-misconduct investigations.

climate.basis: Supports transit expansion to 'tackle the climate crisis'; no carbon-pricing position.

healthcare.basis: Vision includes 'universal coverage, prioritizing patients over profits', mechanism unspecified.

social.basis: Supports the reproductive-care Shield Law; endorsed by Pro-Choice Washington.

parental-rights.basis: Voted yes on ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parents' rights law; no campaign statement on the topic.

experience.basis: Sitting legislator with committee leadership and enacted bills; tenure length not documented in the dossier.

candidates.summary: Independent first-time candidate with decades in the Lake Washington Education Association and sports officiating, running against party-line politics.
highlights: Proposes a voluntary state registration credential for undocumented residents, with limits on transfers to ICE [S1][S4]
Proposes a 50% assessment on political contributions to fund voter information [S4]
Would cut B&O taxes on small businesses and says the capital gains tax should be 'reconsidered by voters' [S4]

taxes.basis: Would reduce the B&O tax on small businesses and put the capital gains tax back to voters.

spending.basis: Calls for fiscal accountability and 'a government that listens to citizens before it spends their money'.

housing.basis: Permitting streamlining and preserving single-family zoning, alongside rent caps in mixed-income housing and landlord incentives.

safety.basis: Wants misdemeanors enforced and repeat offenders prosecuted, paired with treatment and housing.

local-control.basis: Would modify HB 1110's state multifamily zoning mandate and give school districts more authority over graduation standards.

reform.basis: Runs as an independent against party-line politics and proposes a 50% assessment on political contributions.

immigration.basis: Supports a state credential for qualifying undocumented residents and a warrant requirement for ICE transfers, excluding new arrivals and people with felonies.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with no elected experience.
